walkthrough:
Set the derivative equal to zero to locate the stationary minimum point $A$ for $x > 0$:
$$2x - \frac{2}{x^3} = 0 \implies 2x = \frac{2}{x^3} \implies 2x^4 = 2 \implies x^4 = 1$$
$$x_A = 1 \quad (\text{since } x > 0)$$

hints: Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 2x^{-3}$ to get $f(x) = x^2 + x^{-2} + c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate the derivative with respect to $x$:
$$f(x) = \int (2x - 2x^{-3})\,dx = x^2 - 2\left(\frac{x^{-2}}{-2}\right) + c = x^2 + x^{-2} + c = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} + c$$

Substitute the known point $\left(4, \frac{189}{16}\right)$ to determine $c$:
$$\frac{189}{16} = 4^2 + \frac{1}{4^2} + c = 16 + \frac{1}{16} + c = \frac{257}{16} + c$$
$$c = \frac{189}{16} - \frac{257}{16} = -\frac{68}{16} = -\frac{17}{4}$$
$$f(x) = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} - \frac{17}{4} \quad \left(\text{or } x^2 + x^{-2} - \frac{17}{4}\right)$$

Multiply by $4x^2$ to form a quadratic in $x^2$:
$$4x^4 - 17x^2 + 4 = 0$$

Factorise and solve for positive $x$ values:
$$(4x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4) = 0$$
$$x^2 = \frac{1}{4} \implies x_B = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$x^2 = 4 \implies x_C = 2$$
$$x_B = \frac{1}{2}, \quad x_C = 2$$

Set up the definite integral for the region between the curve and the $x$-axis from $x = \frac{1}{2}$ to $x = 2$ (noting the curve lies below the $x$-axis):
$$\text{Integral} = \int_{1/2}^2 \left(x^2 + x^{-2} - \frac{17}{4}\right) dx = \left[ \frac{x^3}{3} - \frac{1}{x} - \frac{17x}{4} \right]_{1/2}^2$$

Subtract and take the absolute value for the shaded area:
$$\text{Area} = \left| -\frac{19}{3} - \left(-\frac{49}{12}\right) \right| = \left| -\frac{76 - 49}{12} \right| = \left| -\frac{27}{12} \right| = \frac{9}{4} \quad \left(= 2\frac{1}{4} = 2.25\right)$$
